L156@P2: Theorem 4.1. The algorithm above returns PRIME if and only if n is prime.
L157@P2: In the remainder of the section, we establish this theorem through a sequence of lemmas. The following
L158@P2: is trivial:
L159@P2: Lemma 4.2. If n is prime, the algorithm returns PRIME.
L160@P2: Proof. If n is prime then steps 1 and 3 can never return COMPOSITE. By Lemma 2.1, the for loop
L161@P2: also cannot return COMPOSITE. Therefore the algorithm will identify n as PRIME either in step 4 or
L162@P2: in step 6.
L163@P2: The converse of the above lemma requires a little more work. If the algorithm returns PRIME in
L164@P2: step 4 then n must be prime since otherwise step 3 would have found a non-trivial factor of n. So the only
